The write refusals therefore hold today for the wrong reason, and the allowed `~` write inside `src/app/**` is refused. (2) The guard refuses an absolute Glob pattern under T's acceptance folder (with no `path`), but not the `~` form. (3) After my commit, `git status` shows untracked root entries: `.bashrc`, `.bash_profile`, `.profile`, `.zshrc`, `.zprofile`, `.gitconfig`, `.gitmodules`, `.mcp.json`, `.ripgreprc`, `.idea`, `.vscode`, `docs/source`. Each is a character device 1,3 (`/dev/null`) owned by `nobody`: placeholders the session sandbox mounts, not files I made. I left them alone and committed nothing but the two suite files. (4) No existing case asserts the opposite of either behaviour; I searched every suite for `-B -m pytest`, `coverage run` and `-m coverage`.
risks: The `~` folder is `~/gov-os-worktrees/W2-95` (the suite's fixture layout), not `~/proj`; the README states this. The item-2 cases ask the guard only, and nothing runs, so they say nothing about whether `coverage` is installed in a session's environment.
lessons: The suite's `Call` objects hold a dict, so they cannot be dict keys; pair them in lists. `Path(project) / "."` drops the `.`, so a root-path case needs no special handling. A whole-suite run takes about 3 minutes and fits one foreground command.
